title: Diagnostic: Class Has No Initializers
hints: A subclass inherits its parent's initialisers only if its new stored properties have defaults.
jsBridge: A class with a stored property that has no default and no initialiser doesn't compile. Swift insists every property is set before use. JS leaves it `undefined`, and TS's `strictPropertyInitialization` is an opt-in version of the same check.

compass.q: TS `strictPropertyInitialization` catches this, and `!` silences it. What's Swift's equivalent escape hatch (`!` IUOs), and why is it discouraged?
Structs get a memberwise init for free. Why don't classes?
Which initialisers does a subclass inherit automatically? (Rules 1 and 2 of initialiser inheritance.)
